To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new open source dataset format, and a corresponding software environment for reading this format, which allows for synchronized playback of multi-sensor and -camera streams recorded in real traffic scenarios.

we developed a new open format for synchronized multi-camera and multi-sensor data, which can be used to record long sequences of synchronized multi-camera data, and we created an experimental setup and recorded a large dataset of multi-sensor and omni-camera sequences.

we present a new open source multi-sensor traffic scene dataset that includes synchronized omnidirectional multi-view video, and a software environment for reading and analyzing these data sets, which will be made available to the public.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of methods for the perception of dynamic traffic scenes.
the development of a multi-sensor dataset with omnidirectional video and a software environment for reading and processing these data sets.
the development of a multi-sensor dataset that is time-shaped and provides high frame rate omnidirectional video streams.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we provide the community with a new open source data format and an open source reader, and a collection of long, synchronized, multi-sensor data sequences recorded in various traffic environments.
the dataset described in this paper is the first of its kind, i.e., it is the first dataset with synchronized multi-sensor and omni-directional video data.
the presented data set and software environment will be an important contribution to the research community working on the development of intelligent and safe vehicles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a multi-sensor traffic scene dataset with omnidirectional video.

this dataset can be considered as the first of its kind, which is publicly available, with synchronized and time stamped data streams, recorded from a real moving car, in realistic traffic situations, with high frame rates and with omnidirectional multi-view video.
we provide a novel dataset of synchronized data streams of various sensors and cameras, and we present the first public dataset with omnidirectional video recorded at 60 Hz.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the data format is designed to allow for easy and efficient processing of multi-sensor recordings, while the data set itself can be used for training and testing of perception and localization algorithms.
the data collection and the format design should be driven by the application requirements, which are not always met by existing datasets.
it is possible to record and synchronize data streams from different sources in a way that allows to use the data in the future for training of machine-learning-based perception algorithms.
